name: Framefields
role: Reference: TypeScript film renderer on native WebGPU, no browser, MP4 out
notes: 2026-11-27: Triage: assess. It is the closest rival to VCR's own seek-and-capture route and the only catalogued film engine with no browser. Lead said install via `pnpm dlx framefields init`; onboarding used `pnpm add framefields` in the example instead. The lead said Node >= 22, but its native webcodecs binding declares ^22.20, and pnpm silently skips it on 22.19.

2026-11-27: Verdict keep as reference, not core: VCR's decisions (ADR 0001, in-house engine) stand. It brings its own Composition model, audio, vision models and a hosted AI gateway (FRAMEFIELDS_API_KEY, keep out of any VCR route) and about 27 MB of dependencies including onnxruntime and skia-canvas. Two major versions in six weeks. The optional SAM 3 weights are under the Meta SAM License, not Apache-2.0.

2026-11-27: Versus hyperframes, revideo and motion-canvas: they seek a DOM or canvas in a browser; framefields renders frame-addressed WebGPU in Node (24 frames at about 114 fps on an M3 Pro) and was hash-identical across order and reruns. Versus VCR capture: no DOM, CSS or web fonts, so VCR scenes cannot move over; use it when a scene is native 3D, effects or compositing, not for DOM layout.

evidence.result: 320x180 12fps 24-frame composition; 5 probe frames raw RGBA 230400 bytes, 4 distinct hashes; shuffled equals sequential; two runs byte-identical; MP4 h264 320x180 24 frames; no engine errors; Node v22.19.0, about 114 fps
evidence.scope: framefields 3.0.2 in Node on macOS arm64: frame-addressed WebGPU render and h264 MP4, deterministic across order and reruns. Not 3D, effects, audio, vision, other GPUs or MP4 bytes.

summary: TypeScript code-first film engine that renders frames natively on WebGPU (Dawn/Metal/Vulkan) in Node, with no browser, and encodes MP4 with audio. A Composition holds layers (flex boxes, Slug vector text, video, 3D, effects) animated by GSAP-style easing; any frame is rendered by index, so scenes are seekable and deterministic. Ships a CLI, component registry, preview server and an optional hosted AI gateway.
use_when: A film or 3D/effects-heavy motion piece should render with no browser, faster than seek-and-capture
Frame-addressed GPU compositing is needed in Node, which revideo and hyperframes do via a browser
Studying a competing code-first film model before deciding what VCR's own engine should borrow
avoid_when: Use VCR's browser capture route when the scene needs DOM layout, CSS or web fonts
Use motion-canvas for editor-driven 2D explainers with a large ecosystem and slower release pace
Use dawn-node-webgpu directly when only WebGPU readback is needed, without a film framework

assessment.rationale: npm 3.0.2 (2026-11-13), repo pushed 2026-11-18, Apache-2.0. Unique in the catalogue as a no-browser GPU film engine, with a passing determinism fixture. Young (first release 2026-10-05), heavy dependencies, hosted gateway and SAM 3 licence stay outside VCR.
